title: The purpose of tailoring
blurb: Explain why PRINCE2 is tailored and the two things tailoring is meant to achieve.
question: A project board for a small, low-risk project agrees to receive shorter highlight reports every two weeks instead of detailed weekly ones. Which principle is being applied, and what is its purpose?

teach.h: Tailoring: fitting the method to the project
teach.body: Formally, 'tailor to suit the project' is the seventh principle: PRINCE2 is applied and adapted to suit the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk. In plain English, every PRINCE2 project uses the same method, but the amount of paperwork, reporting and ceremony is set to match the job in hand. A two-week office refit and a five-year hospital build both use PRINCE2, just not in the same way.

teach.caption: Purpose 1: the management method suits the project (for example aligned with the business processes that govern it). Purpose 2: project controls suit its scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk.

teach.body: PRINCE2 is used on projects of every size and in every sector, so it cannot prescribe one exact way of working. Instead of dictating how to align the method with each project, it gives guidance through its seven principles. The result is that the method is applied differently on different projects, even inside one organization, while the principles stay the same everywhere.

teach.caption: The principles are the foundation of the five integrated elements. What sits on top is shaped to fit the project; the foundation is not.

teach.h: Controls that scale with the project
head: Control
Small, low-risk project
Large, high-risk project
teach.caption: Illustrative contrasts. The rule is proportion: the frequency and formality of controls follow the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk.

teach.h: Worked scenario: two projects, one council
teach.body: At Fernbrook District Council, project manager Aisha Mensah runs a six-week project to install two self-service kiosks in a library. She proposes initiation plus one delivery stage and short fortnightly highlight emails. Her colleague Tom Varga manages a two-year housing system replacement with many suppliers. His board wants several delivery stages, weekly formal highlight reports and fuller risk reviews. Both projects are tailored correctly: each set of controls fits its project.

teach.h: Getting the level of control right

bands.label: Board loses sight of progress and risk
Controls match scale, complexity and risk
Effort wasted on reports nobody needs

teach.caption: Tailoring protects against both failures: a heavy method on a small job, and a thin method on a risky one.

rows.label: More frequent reports for an inexperienced team
Virtual highlight reports for a dispersed board
Using the organization's own project terms
Dropping 'manage by exception' to save time
Project manager also acting as executive

teach.note: Tailoring changes how the method is applied. It never removes a principle or a role rule.

teach.text: Tailoring is about proportion, not omission. Changing terms, merging documents, adding a coach or adjusting report frequency is tailoring. Leaving out a principle is not: if any of the seven principles is not applied, the project is not a PRINCE2 project.

items: 'Tailor to suit the project' is one of the seven principles (2.7).
Purpose 1: the method used is appropriate to the project, for example aligned with its business processes.
Purpose 2: project controls suit the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk.
Typical controls tailored: the frequency and formality of reports and reviews.
The principles are the fixed base; how the method is applied varies from project to project.

summary: You can now explain why PRINCE2 is tailored and state its two purposes: making the method suit the project and making controls proportionate to its scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk. You can also tell proportionate tailoring apart from dropping a principle.

A.q: Which is a purpose of tailoring PRINCE2 to a project?
options: To make every project use the same reporting frequency
To let the project board omit principles of little value
To make project controls suit the project's scale and risk
To pass accountability for the business case to the PM
A.why: One purpose of tailoring is that project controls are appropriate to the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk (2.7).

whyNot.0: Tailoring does the opposite: reporting frequency is set to suit each project, so it varies.
whyNot.1: Principles cannot be tailored away. All seven must be applied for the project to be PRINCE2.
whyNot.3: The executive owns the business case. Tailoring does not move that accountability.

A.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. Under the 'tailor to suit the project' principle, PRINCE2 is adapted to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and [?].
options: funding source
level of risk
contract type
sponsor's seniority
A.why: The seven tailoring factors are environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk (2.7).

whyNot.0: Funding source is not one of the seven named tailoring factors.
whyNot.2: A contract may be an influence through the commercial context, but 'contract type' is not one of the seven named factors.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 has no sponsor role, and seniority is not a tailoring factor.

A.q: Why does PRINCE2 give guidance through principles rather than prescribing exactly how to align the method with each project?
options: So that each organization runs one fixed project approach
So that it replaces the industry-specific models in use
So that the project board can choose which principles apply
So that the method can be applied to suit each project
A.why: Because PRINCE2 is used on so many kinds of project, it guides through principles; the method is then applied differently on different projects, even within one organization (ch 2).

whyNot.0: The principles lead to different applications on different projects, even inside one organization.
whyNot.1: PRINCE2 works alongside specialist industry models; it does not replace them.
whyNot.2: All seven principles apply to every PRINCE2 project; the board cannot select among them.

B.q: The board of a small, low-risk office move agrees to receive short highlight reports by email every two weeks instead of formal weekly reports. What does this show?
options: Tailoring project controls to the project's scale and risk
Managing by exception through narrower stage tolerances
Removing the progress practice from a small project
Changing the project's delivery approach to iterative
B.why: Adjusting the frequency and formality of reports to suit the project's scale and risk is a purpose of tailoring (2.7).

whyNot.1: No tolerances have changed. The change is to how often and how formally the board is informed.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports are still produced, so the progress practice is still applied, just more lightly.
whyNot.3: Reporting frequency says nothing about the delivery approach; the work itself is unchanged.

B.q:
Which two statements about the purpose of tailoring are correct?
1. It makes the management method used appropriate to the project.
2. It makes project controls appropriate to the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk.
3. It allows a principle to be set aside on a small project.
4. It removes the need for the board to agree how the method is applied.
options: 1 and 3
2 and 4
1 and 2
3 and 4
B.why: The two purposes of tailoring are that the method suits the project and that its controls suit the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk (2.7).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: principles are not tailored, whatever the project's size.
whyNot.1: Statement 4 is false: tailoring must be documented and agreed, and the board approves it in the PID.
whyNot.3: Both statements are false: principles stay, and the board agrees the tailoring.

B.q: A high-importance, high-risk infrastructure project has a team that is new to project work. How should tailoring affect its controls?
options: Lighter controls, because the board members are senior
Controls copied from the organization's smallest project
More frequent and more formal controls are likely
Controls set separately by each team manager
B.why: Controls are tailored to importance, risk and team capability, so a risky project with an inexperienced team is likely to need more frequent, more formal reporting and review (2.7).

whyNot.0: Board seniority is not a tailoring factor; the project's risk and team capability point to tighter control.
whyNot.1: Copying a small project's controls ignores this project's importance and risk.
whyNot.3: Project controls are agreed between the project manager and the board, not set team by team.

C.q: Which statement about tailoring is correct?
options: It adapts the principles while the processes stay fixed
It adapts how the method is applied; all principles remain
It is done by the business layer before the mandate
It suits small projects; large ones use PRINCE2 untailored
C.why: Tailoring changes how the method is applied (processes, practices, roles, products, terms) while all seven principles must still be applied (2.0, 2.7).

whyNot.0: It is the reverse: principles are fixed, and processes can be combined, simplified or done in more detail.
whyNot.2: The project manager leads 'agree the tailoring requirements' in initiating a project, after the mandate.
whyNot.3: Every PRINCE2 project is tailored, large or small; the principle applies to all of them.

C.q: At Calderbrook Hospital Trust, the project manager proposes calling stages 'phases' and highlight reports 'weekly updates' to match the trust's own terms. Which principle is being applied, and what is being tailored?
options: Tailor to suit the project; the terminology
Focus on products; the management products
Define roles and relationships; the roles
Learn from experience; the processes
C.why: Using the organization's own terms is tailoring of terminology under the 'tailor to suit the project' principle (2.7).

whyNot.1: Focus on products is about defining products and their quality criteria, not renaming method terms.
whyNot.2: No roles or responsibilities are changing; only the names of a stage and a report.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience is about seeking and applying lessons, and no process is being changed here.

C.q: Which is NOT a reason for tailoring PRINCE2 to a project?
options: To align the method with business processes that govern it
To set reporting frequency to suit the team's capability
To use project terms that are familiar in the organization
To cut down the number of principles a small project uses
C.why: Principles cannot be tailored: all seven apply to every PRINCE2 project, whatever its size (2.0).

whyNot.0: Aligning the method with the business processes that govern and support the project is a stated purpose of tailoring.
whyNot.1: Reporting frequency suited to team capability is a classic example of proportionate tailoring.
whyNot.2: Tailoring terminology to the organization's own terms is allowed.

reteach.title: Think of a tailored suit
reteach.question: A tailor uses the same pattern for every customer but cuts each suit to fit. What stays fixed in PRINCE2, and what gets cut to fit?

blocks.body: The pattern is PRINCE2's seven principles: every suit has them, or it is not a PRINCE2 suit. The cut is everything else: how many stages, how often and how formally the board hears about progress, what the reports are called, how detailed the plans are. A tailor who left out a sleeve would not be tailoring; neither is a project that drops a principle.

blocks.text: The purpose of tailoring is fit and proportion: the method suits the project, and the controls suit its scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk. It is never a licence to skip a principle.

explain.h: Purpose 1: the method fits the project
explain.body: The management method should suit the project and the organization around it, for example by aligning PRINCE2 with the business processes that govern and support the project, or by using the organization's own terms.

explain.h: From standard method to fitted method

test.q: Aligning the project's management method with the business processes that govern and support it is a purpose of what?
options: Quality assurance
Change management
Project assurance
Tailoring
test.why: Making the method appropriate to the project, for example aligned with its governing business processes, is one of the two purposes of tailoring (2.7).

whyNot.0: Quality assurance independently checks that quality procedures are in place and followed.
whyNot.1: In PRINCE2 7, change management means helping people move to new ways of working.
whyNot.2: Project assurance gives the board independent checks on the project; aligning the method with business processes is the aim of tailoring.

explain.body: Project controls should be in proportion to the project's scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk. The classic examples are how often reports and reviews happen and how formal they are.

test.q: Which is an example of tailoring project controls?
options: Combining the executive and project manager roles
Changing the frequency and formality of reports
Leaving out the business case on a compulsory project
Replacing the seven principles with company rules
test.why: Adjusting how often and how formally reports and reviews happen is the standard example of tailoring project controls (2.7).

whyNot.0: The executive and project manager roles cannot be combined, so this breaks a role rule.
whyNot.2: Compulsory projects still need business justification, at least for the chosen option.
whyNot.3: The principles cannot be replaced or tailored away.

explain.body: All seven principles must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project. Tailoring works on everything built on top of them, never on the principles themselves.

test.q: A project applies six of the seven PRINCE2 principles. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a PRINCE2 project tailored for its size
It is a PRINCE2 project if the board agrees
It is not a PRINCE2 project
It is a PRINCE2 project if the PID records it
test.why: A project is a PRINCE2 project only when all seven principles are applied (ch 2).

whyNot.0: Size can change how the method is applied, but it cannot remove a principle.
whyNot.1: The board cannot approve dropping a principle; tailoring works on the method, not the principles.
whyNot.3: Recording a missing principle in the PID does not make the project PRINCE2.

explain.body: More control is not always better. Heavy reporting on a tiny project wastes effort, while light reporting on a risky project leaves the board blind. Tailoring aims for controls that match the project.

test.q: A project manager uses the full set of formal weekly reports for a two-person, one-month internal project. What is the main concern?
options: The controls are out of proportion to its scale
It breaks the 'manage by stages' principle
The reports should go to the business layer
The board has lost its authority to direct
test.why: Controls should be proportionate to scale, complexity, importance, team capability and risk; this level of formality is excessive for so small a project (2.7).

whyNot.1: Manage by stages concerns stages as decision points; heavy reporting does not breach it.
whyNot.2: Highlight reporting goes to the project board, not the business layer.
whyNot.3: Extra reporting does not reduce the board's authority; the problem is wasted effort.
